scenario_summary: Customer is requesting a refund for a service subscription canceled 34 days ago, which is slightly outside the standard 30-day refund window.

conversation.message: Hi, my name is Tyrone Jackson and I'm 76. I'm trying to get a refund for a service I canceled 34 days ago. I know your refund policy is usually 30 days, but I was traveling and only just saw the charge — I didn't realize it had gone through until now. Is there anything you can do?

Hello, Mr. Jackson. I understand how frustrating it is to return from travel and see an unexpected charge for a service you had already canceled. I would be happy to look into this for you. To get started, could you please provide your account number and the email address associated with your subscription?
Sure, my account number is 8829-4410 and the email is t.jackson@email.com.

Thank you for that information. I have successfully verified your account. I see here that the cancellation was processed on the 34th day following the renewal charge. Under our 'Subscription Billing Policy 4.2', refunds are typically restricted to requests made within 30 days of the billing date. However, given your long-standing history with us and the circumstances you've described, I have the authority to make a one-time exception.
Oh, that would be wonderful. I really appreciate you taking the time to look into this for me.

It is my pleasure, Mr. Jackson. I have processed the refund for the $49.99 charge back to your original payment method. You should see the credit reflect in your account within 3 to 5 business days, depending on your financial institution. Is there anything else I can assist you with today?
No, that was exactly what I needed. Thank you so much for your help.

resolution_summary: Agent verified the account and applied a one-time policy exception to process a full refund for the subscription charge, despite the request falling outside the standard 30-day window.
